summary: LLMs trained to perform explicit multi-step reasoning before answering, using chain-of-thought to solve complex problems

content.overview: Reasoning models (also called Large Reasoning Models or LRMs) are LLMs specifically trained to perform explicit step-by-step reasoning before generating answers. Unlike standard LLMs that immediately respond, reasoning models use 'chain-of-thought' (CoT) to break down problems, try different approaches, recognize mistakes, and self-correct. OpenAI's o1 (Sept 2024) and o3 (Dec 2024) pioneered this approach, trained via reinforcement learning to spend 'thinking time' solving problems. Critical insight: Performance scales with both train-time compute (RL training) and test-time compute (thinking duration).
keyPoints: Chain-of-Thought (CoT): Models internally generate step-by-step reasoning (often hidden from user) before final answer - mimics human deliberation
CRITICAL DISTINCTION: Standard LLMs respond immediately; reasoning models 'think' (extend inference time) to explore solution paths before answering
Training via Reinforcement Learning (RL): Models learn to refine reasoning strategies, recognize errors, break complex steps into simpler ones, try alternative approaches
Test-time compute scaling: More thinking time → better accuracy (o3: 75.7% on ARC-AGI with low compute, 87.5% with high compute)
o3 benchmarks (2025): 87.5% ARC-AGI (3x improvement over o1), 25% Frontier Math (vs. 2% previous best), 96.7% AIME math competition
Cost-performance tradeoff: o3-mini is 15x cheaper and 5x faster than o1 with comparable performance for everyday tasks
Competition: DeepSeek R1 (open-source) rivals OpenAI o1/o3; Anthropic Claude 3.7+ offers 'extended thinking' (similar approach, token budget control)
CRITICAL: All reasoning approaches (o1/o3, Claude extended thinking, DeepSeek R1) use tokens for internal reasoning - charged as output tokens

examples.title: Reasoning Model Workflow
examples.explanation: Reasoning models perform extensive internal deliberation before responding - latency increases but accuracy improves

warnings: COST: Reasoning models generate many internal reasoning tokens (charged as output tokens). OpenAI o1: $60/M output vs $15/M for GPT-4. You pay for hidden reasoning + final answer.
CRITICAL: Extended thinking (Anthropic) and reasoning (OpenAI) BOTH use tokens for internal thinking - you ARE charged for these tokens as output tokens
LATENCY: Responses take longer (seconds to minutes for complex problems) - unsuitable for real-time, low-latency applications
Reasoning is often HIDDEN - o1/o3 don't expose full chain-of-thought by default, making debugging and verification harder (Claude and o3-mini expose more)
Budget control varies: Claude allows token budget limits for thinking (min 1,024 tokens), OpenAI o1/o3 have no user-controllable budget for reasoning
NOT a silver bullet - reasoning models excel at logic, math, coding but don't fundamentally solve hallucination or bias problems
Chain-of-thought can be hijacked - recent research (H-CoT attack, 2025) shows reasoning safety checks can be manipulated via jailbreaks
Over-application is wasteful - use reasoning models for complex problems requiring deliberation, not simple queries (use standard LLMs for those)
bestPractices: Use reasoning models for: Complex math, competitive programming, scientific reasoning, multi-step logic problems, debugging
Use standard LLMs for: Simple queries, content generation, summarization, chat, real-time responses
Choose compute level based on task: Low compute (o3-mini) for everyday tasks, high compute (o3) for hardest problems
When available, enable reasoning trace visibility (o3-mini feature) to verify logic and debug failures
Budget for increased cost and latency - reasoning models are 10-100x more expensive and slower than standard LLMs
Combine with tools - reasoning models plan and strategize, tools execute (database queries, calculations, API calls)
